candidates.place_reason: 306e audit 2026-10-13: similarity (6 points, resid 0.0 m, 1.00 m/px, -0.0 deg) - the 6 anchors are a 100-px diagonal ladder (100,100)..(600,600) that pins the 1280x1551 plate centre onto the site point; no placement information. The 1836 Penny Magazine plate is a genuine plan of the Stanton Drew circle group (Great Circle, Circle of 8, South-west Circle, The Cove, Hackett's Quoit, River Chew - the right names and layout against the 1842 six-inch and the LiDAR) drawn at ~10 m/px: the fitted 1.0 m/px inflates the group ~4-10x. The drawn Great Circle (least-squares r=218 px = 435 m across, centre E+157 N-153) surrounds the real stone cluster (~50 m of dots at E+100-150 N-50) about 90 m south of it; the drawn Circle of 8 (E-91 N+240) and South-west Circle (E+705 N-554) sit on open farmland where the 1842 and the LiDAR show no stones (the real SW circle lies near Church Farm, E-100 N-200). Wrong size, and the secondary circles miss the real ones. Document deleted.
